§7.2 · FUEL CAPTURE · TWO ENTERED, ONE COMPUTED
The custom in-sheet keypad with a locale decimal key is not a nicety: the system keyboard cannot be trusted to offer ,, and money parsing is a 1000× corruption class. 1.234,56 = 1,234.56 = 1234,56, and grouping-only 20.000 is 20000, never 20,0.

The derived pill is visibly derived

Lighter fill, ink-soft value, and the word computed under it. It is not a normal field wearing the same clothes. The two entered pills wear the accent wash, so which numbers are yours is readable at a glance.

Arithmetic: 35,75 ÷ 26,10 = 1,3697… displayed as 1,370. The rounding lives only in the display of the derived value — neither typed number is touched. Never rounding a user's typed value to make the third come out even is the whole rule.

And the well says +132, while this fill measures over 378. Both are right, and they answer different questions: the well's delta is since the last reading of any kind (the 8 July service, 91.108), the economy interval is since the last full tank (the 2 July fill, 90.862). A well that reported the economy interval would be lying about how far the car has gone since it was last looked at.

The derived-pill state machine

ENTERED
SCREEN
nothing
three empty pills, none marked, Save disabled
one value
nothing is computable yet; no pill marked; Save disabled
two values
the third computes live and is marked computed
user edits the computed pill
it becomes entered; the least-recently-edited of the other two becomes the new computed one. Your last two edits win — predictable, and it never silently discards what was just typed
user clears a pill
its computed neighbour stays computed if two values remain; otherwise all marks drop

Defaults that earn the ten seconds

Full tank defaults ON — the common case, and the one that measures. Station is a menu with recents first, then New station, then none. The date pill is backdatable and never future. Save stays disabled until total + litres exist, entered or computed. The car picker renders only when a second car exists.

02 · The odometer well, in all five states

Every capture surface reuses this well, edits included — so these five states are the app's whole odometer behaviour, not one screen's.
FIRST READING EVER
91.240km
Koi will measure from here.
No delta to state, so it states the consequence instead of showing a dash.
HARD STOP · NAMES THE CONFLICT
90.100km
A reading on 12 July says 91.240 km.
Open that record
Critical text on the ordinary surface — the field takes a critical border, nothing turns red. And it offers the door to the conflicting record rather than just refusing.
SOFT · A JUMP OVER 5.000 KM
97.400km
+6.160 km since the last reading.
Does that look right?
Save anyway Go back
Asks, does not block. A soft-confirmed value is saved as typed, never adjusted afterwards.
LEFT EMPTY · FULL TANK ON
km
Without an odometer this fill still counts. Its litres join the next measured interval.
The single easiest thing to get wrong. The fill saves fine, contributes its litres, and produces no economy number of its own — and the sheet says so at entry, rather than letting the user discover it in a chart.
EDITING THIS FILL'S OWN READING
91.180km
Editing a saved reading. Correcting it down or up is always allowed here.
Inv. 10. The edit excludes the record's own reading and its folded twin from validation — without it, noticing a mistyped digit after saving would be permanently blocked by a check naming the record's own value as "the conflict".

03 · The saved moment — the app's only spring

Auto-dismisses in ~2 s. Reduce-motion gets a fade. The moment must never claim a number it does not have.

§7.3 · THE SAVED MOMENT · MEASURED
SIX VARIANTS · THE MOMENT NEVER CLAIMS A NUMBER IT DOES NOT HAVE
CASE
COPY
measured
Saved. Economy computed. + the number + over 378 km
first fill · chain not started
Saved. + Two full tanks measure your first number.
partial fill
Saved. + Economy resumes at the next full tank.
full, no odometer
Saved. + Add the odometer to measure this interval. — the same sentence the record page uses, since the interval is not lost: that page offers ( Add the odometer ) on this exact fill
missed previous
Saved. + That interval isn't measured.
an edit
no ceremony at all — saves quietly, sheet closes. Ceremony is for creation

The spring is for the record, not the user

Not a badge, not a streak, not a "nice work". That distinction is what separates feedback from gamification, and it is why this one spring can exist in an app that refuses all the others.

A number, not a verdict

The moment shows 6,9 L/100km and its interval — never "better than last time". Comparison belongs on the record page and in Insights, where the basis is visible.

One odometer surface with two doors. A trip that refuses surveillance. A note that carries no amount.

A chip fills the note field and leaves it editable. There is no stored category taxonomy — a constitutional refusal — and the chips exist because verbose free-text notes ruined the ranked cost rows. Service adds an odometer field; expense does not.

Readings are checked against your ledger.
Refuses: GPS, background tracking, a timer, per-trip economy, average speed. A trip is two odometer readings and a name, not surveillance — and a 13-hour trip showing "57 km/h" is parked-time fiction.
Both figures carry ≈ and name their basis. The double-count disclaimer lives on the trip's record page, where the number is being read as a total; here, at your averages is the honest label. An unknown end shows the card without a km figure rather than showing 0 km.

§7.7 · GUARDS ON EVERY CAPTURE SHEET
GUARD
BEHAVIOUR
dirty guard
the sheet pins and asks Discard this fill? / Keep editing. Swipe-to-close disabled while dirty
soft validation
warn + Save anyway / Go back: odometer jump > 5.000 km · litres > tank × 1,15 · €/L outside 0,60…3,50
hard validation
blocks and names the conflict: monotonicity either direction · odometer outside 0…9.999.999 · litres ≤ 0 · amount ≤ 0
the edit exclusion
on an edit, the record's own reading and any folded twin are excluded from the monotonicity check — the hard stop applies to new readings only
never
silently fixing anything afterwards. A soft-confirmed value is saved as typed, not adjusted
money parsing
locale-safe: 1.234,56 = 1,234.56 = 1234,56, and grouping-only 20.000 is 20000, never 20,0
hard error styling
the message is critical text; the surface never turns red

Client and server run the same pure functions

The architecture's flag, never fix posture means the server would accept and flag a bad write — so refusing it here is what keeps the user's own device honest without repairing anything silently. Already true in the build for odometer readings; every new capture surface inherits it.

The one gesture the dirty guard outranks

A notification deep-link's modal teardown. A half-typed fill is unrecoverable; a notification is still sitting in Notification Center. The guard wins, and the deep link waits.

Sheet 07 of 07 — batch 1 complete. The reconciliation ledger and the open-question log ship alongside as decisions.md. Batch 2 picks up History, Insights' four lenses, record pages, reminders, the vault and onboarding.
